published_source: Table 9 col 6, paper_results.log (authors' Stata log shipped in the package; no article text or PDF in the project) lines 2155-2500; fixest reproduction matches to 3 decimals, N = 10045.
notes: Zip-code x month panel (timeperiod 8-34), 773 zips, unbalanced. Treatment policy_entry (Airbnb Plus available in the zip), absorbing, 6 adoption cohorts (14:29 zips, 22:127, 23:1, 26:2, 28:1, 32:1), 612 never-treated zips, no always-treated, no switch-offs. Controls: nine annual ACS covariates (acs_ctrls) that update at calendar-year breaks, entered linearly as published. xtreg fe with i.timeperiod, cluster(zipcode), unweighted. Only violation of PROTOCOL Section 2: time-varying controls (5c). Sample: rows with non-missing average_booked_nights. CEM-matched sample (zips with total_weights != 0), estimated UNWEIGHTED as in the authors' code: a plain TWFE on a matched sample counts as a sample restriction under PROTOCOL 5b. Nov 2 audit (meta-3): gvar g_entry -> g_true and data_path -> airbnbplus_prepared_v2_gtrue.csv (same rows and columns plus g_true), for consistency with the event spec T5c1 and PROTOCOL ruling (b). For 5 zips (20782, 37064, 70005, 80011 -> 22; 94130 -> 14) the authors' relative-time dummies date adoption to the launch month, and the months between launch and the first observed treated row are missing from the panel, so g_entry (first observed treated month: 28, 23, 26, 26, 32) dated them late and created four one- or two-zip cohorts. Treatment on every observed row is unchanged (policy_entry = 1[t >= g_true]), so TWFE and imputation are unchanged; CSA now has two cohorts (14: 30 zips, 22: 131 zips).
data_source_note: Prepared from the shipped airbnbplus_data.dta (column subset, rows unchanged) with g_entry = first timeperiod with policy_entry == 1 in the full zip panel (0 = never). gvar is used instead of treat_var so that six zips whose true first treated month has a missing outcome or control are not dated one month late (prep.R in the work directory).
